title: Per-request KV/prefix cache outcome classification + hit-bytes + saved-prefill-ms counters
creator: Omar El-Sayed
description:
Goal
Add per-request cache outcome classification and counters needed for reliable dashboards/alerts and Optimize recommendations:
- outcome: hit | miss | partial
- hit_bytes (cache bytes re-used for the request)
- saved_prefill_ms (estimated prefill compute time avoided due to cache re-use)

This issue is specifically about: (1) defining/implementing per-request classification logic in the runtime, and (2) emitting request-scoped counters that can be aggregated safely (with sampling controls handled by pipeline).

Context
Telemetry v2 needs to answer:
- “Are we hitting the cache?” (hit rate)
- “How much are we saving?” (hit_bytes, saved_prefill_ms)
- “Are we miscounting partial prefill / multi-step prefill?” (known source of confusion)

This ticket assumes ENG-4813 provides the underlying cache event hooks + request correlation id so we can attribute cache activity to a single request.

Definitions (runtime-side)
Per-request cache outcome is derived from the prefill path only (decode tokens do not participate in prefix/KV cache lookup):
- hit: cache lookup succeeded and covered the entire intended prefix span for the request’s prompt (i.e., no new prefill executed for tokens that were eligible for cache)
- miss: cache lookup failed (no matching prefix) OR lookup succeeded but covered 0 eligible tokens
- partial: lookup succeeded but covered only a strict subset of eligible prefix tokens (requires some prefill work)

Notes:
- “eligible prefix tokens” excludes tokens that are not cacheable by policy (e.g., cache disabled, prompt too short, policy min_prefix_tokens not met, prompt contains non-cacheable segments per normalization rules).
- streaming retries / gateway retry semantics may cause multiple runtime attempts; classification should be per runtime request_id attempt, not “end-user request” unless explicitly correlated upstream.

Counters/fields to emit (request-scoped)
- redwood.kv_cache.request_outcome{outcome=hit|miss|partial} = 1
- redwood.kv_cache.hit_bytes = bytes_reused_from_cache
- redwood.kv_cache.saved_prefill_ms = estimated_ms_saved
- redwood.kv_cache.eligible_prefix_tokens = integer count
- redwood.kv_cache.reused_prefix_tokens = integer count
- redwood.kv_cache.prefill_tokens_executed = integer count (actual prefill work performed)

These are intended to roll up into hit-rate, cacheable prompt ratio, and savings views.

Saved prefill estimation (MVP)
We need a consistent, monotonic estimate that correlates with latency and can be used for regression detection.
Proposed MVP:
- saved_prefill_ms = reused_prefix_tokens * per_token_prefill_ms_estimate
Where per_token_prefill_ms_estimate is derived from runtime timing already captured for prefill (if available) or from a conservative per-model constant table (fallback).

Guardrails:
- Must be >= 0 and clamped to a sane upper bound per request to avoid outliers blowing up aggregates.
- For partial outcomes, saved_prefill_ms counts only the reused portion.
- If timing basis is missing (e.g., prefill timing disabled), emit saved_prefill_ms=0 but still emit hit_bytes and token counts (so we can detect instrumentation gaps).

Feature flag
Emit under telemetry v2 flag (exact name to align with platform flags doc; placeholder):
- runtime.enable_kv_cache_telemetry_v2
When disabled, do not compute classification or saved_prefill_ms on hot path.

References
- Telemetry v2 spec (metric names/tags): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/kv-cache-telemetry-v2-metric-spec.json
- Known misclassification edge cases: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/known-issues/cache-hit-rate-misclassification-known-issues.json
- Dashboard requirements: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/cache-hit-rate-dashboards-definition.json
acceptance_criteria:
Functional
- Per-request outcome (hit/miss/partial) is computed deterministically from eligible_prefix_tokens vs reused_prefix_tokens.
- Runtime emits request-scoped counters/fields: request_outcome, hit_bytes, saved_prefill_ms, eligible_prefix_tokens, reused_prefix_tokens, prefill_tokens_executed.
- saved_prefill_ms is non-negative, bounded, and consistent across runs for the same synthetic scenario.

Correctness
- Unit tests cover:
  - full hit (reused == eligible)
  - miss (reused == 0, eligible > 0)
  - partial (0 < reused < eligible)
  - not cacheable (eligible == 0) → outcome should be miss with eligible=0 (explicitly documented), and saved_prefill_ms=0
- Handles “partial-prefill” edge case without double counting reused tokens.

Performance
- Added overhead remains within runtime instrumentation budget (tracked in ENG-4813); this ticket should not introduce additional per-token allocations or per-request large payloads.

Operability
- All fields are gated behind the telemetry v2 feature flag.
- Metrics are emitted even when saved_prefill_ms can’t be computed (emit 0), so dashboards can detect missing timing basis.
implementation_notes:
Implementation sketch
- Extend request context (or per-request telemetry struct) with:
  - eligible_prefix_tokens
  - reused_prefix_tokens
  - hit_bytes (from cache metadata: block bytes or KV bytes)
  - prefill_tokens_executed
  - prefill_time_ms (if available)
- Compute classification at the end of prefill planning (after cache lookup resolves) and finalize at end of prefill execution (so we can capture actual prefill tokens executed).

Avoiding misclassification
- Ensure reused_prefix_tokens only counts tokens actually served from cache (not merely “found” in lookup if later invalidated).
- If lookup returns a prefix but we fall back due to incompatible model version / quantization profile, treat as miss and set reused=0 (and consider logging a debug counter; see ENG-4818 recs).

hit_bytes definition
- Use bytes of KV reused (preferred) if available; otherwise approximate as reused_prefix_tokens * bytes_per_token(model, dtype, kv_layout).
- Document in code comments what basis is used so pipeline/dashboards can interpret changes.

saved_prefill_ms basis
- Prefer using measured prefill time and measured prefill_tokens_executed to compute per-token estimate: per_token = prefill_time_ms / max(prefill_tokens_executed, 1)
- Then saved_prefill_ms = reused_prefix_tokens * per_token
- If prefill_time_ms not available, fallback per_token from a small table keyed by model family + GPU class (temporary), with a TODO to remove once timing is always on under v2.

Telemetry payload shape
- Emit as counters/gauges only (no per-token spans).
- Do not include raw prompt/prefix identifiers. If we need prefix buckets later, that’s separate (and will go through cardinality review).
testing_plan:
Synthetic workload test matrix (local + perf-canary-friendly)

A) Deterministic unit tests (no GPU)
- Mock cache lookup result and request tokenization:
  1) eligible=128, reused=128 → outcome=hit, saved_prefill_ms>0 when timing basis present
  2) eligible=128, reused=0 → outcome=miss, saved_prefill_ms=0
  3) eligible=128, reused=64 → outcome=partial
  4) eligible=0 (policy disables cache or too-short prompt) → outcome=miss, eligible=0, reused=0
- Verify hit_bytes derivation path (exact if metadata is present; approximate if not).

B) Integration tests (single-node runtime, GPU optional)
- Use a synthetic prompt set with controlled prefixes:
  - 100 requests with identical first 256 tokens → expect near-100% hits after warmup
  - 100 requests with random prefixes → expect near-0% hits
  - Mixed: 50% share a prefix, 50% random → expect partial distribution depending on min_prefix_tokens
- Validate invariants:
  - 0 <= reused_prefix_tokens <= eligible_prefix_tokens
  - prefill_tokens_executed + reused_prefix_tokens ~= total_prefix_tokens_considered (within policy constraints)

C) Regression test hooks
- Provide a fixture emitter mode that writes computed fields to structured logs for diffing in CI.
- Add scenario notes for PERF canary (ENG-4819) so they can assert stability on: hit-rate and saved_prefill_ms distributions.
rollout_notes:
Rollout
- Land behind runtime.enable_kv_cache_telemetry_v2.
- Initially enable only in staging + internal canaries; coordinate with telemetry pipeline changes (ENG-4815) so we don’t spam unrecognized metrics.
- Watch for:
  - saved_prefill_ms unexpectedly zero across all traffic (timing basis missing)
  - partial outcomes spiking (likely miscount or policy change)

Rollback
- Flip flag off; metrics should cease without affecting request execution.
comments: 2025-02-12 (Logan Wright): Please ensure outcome logic matches v2 spec language (eligible vs reused). We need eligible=0 to be explicit so we can compute “cacheable prompt ratio” correctly downstream.

2025-02-14 (Noah Patel): Be careful with counting reused tokens when prefill is split into multiple chunks (scheduler). If we reuse prefix for chunk 1 but chunk 2 falls back, we should still count reused for chunk 1 but keep outcome=partial.
2025-02-18 (Marcus Reed): For overhead: avoid reading high-res timers on every request if flag is off; also avoid atomics on the hot decode path. Prefill-only should be fine.

2025-02-21 (Samir Qureshi): Implemented classification + counters behind flag; added unit tests for hit/miss/partial and eligible=0 case. Working on saved_prefill_ms fallback when prefill timing unavailable.
2025-02-24 (Omar El-Sayed): Reviewed changes; requested clamp on saved_prefill_ms and a comment clarifying hit_bytes basis (KV bytes vs approximation). After that, OK to ship to runtime canary.
